1#main: Prohibition of bathing and anointing for a mourner. And it contains 6 seifim. Bathing — how so? Forbidden to bathe his entire body even in cold water; but his face, hands, and feet in hot water are forbidden, in cold permitted; and if he was soiled with mud and excrement he bathes as usual and need not be concerned: {Rama: And all this is by law forbidden only seven days, but afterward bathing is permitted; but nowadays the custom is to forbid all bathing all thirty days (Maharam Laws of Joy and in Hagahot Maimoniyot chapter 7 Laws of Festivals and chapter 10 Laws of Mourning); and even to wash the head is forbidden (below siman 390 and in Avraham Zacuto); and one should not change the custom, for it is an ancient custom founded by elders (Avraham Zacuto in the name of Rashba).}
2#main: Anointing — how so? Forbidden to anoint even any amount if intended for pleasure; but if to remove filth — permitted; and one need not say it is for healing, such as if he has boils on his head.
3#main: A woman who gave birth while mourning and needs to bathe — permitted; and likewise one who has dizziness in his head — permitted to wash his head in hot water, for it is no worse than an asthenic person (meaning: one whose body is cold and chilled) who is permitted to bathe his entire body; and not everyone who says he is asthenic do we permit, only one known to be asthenic who conducts himself with delicacy; and if he does not bathe he will suffer greatly and come to illness.
4#main: One whom his mournings pressed upon him, two mournings one after another — permitted to bathe his entire body in cold water.
5#main: A niddah whose immersion time occurred on her mourning days — she does not immerse: {Rama: (Tur in the name of Rabbenu Tam and according to Mahariq root 35);} and all the more she does not bathe to wear white garments; but immediately after seven, even though bathing is customarily forbidden all thirty, nevertheless she is permitted, only she should change the bathing somewhat (Avraham Zacuto end of Laws of Mourning); and she should wear a white shirt and spread a white sheet so she not come to doubt (responsum of Maharil siman 15).}
6#main: A woman may not apply kohl or rouge on her mourning days, for all these are forbidden like bathing; and a married woman is forbidden only within seven, but after seven permitted in all that she not become repulsive to her husband; a bride who suffered mourning within thirty days of her wedding may adorn herself even within seven; a mature woman who suffered mourning, since she is about to marry, permitted in kohl and rouge; but forbidden in hot bathing of her entire body; a young girl mourning is forbidden even in kohl and rouge.
